title: Inquest into 2018 Departure Bay police shooting begins
subtitle: Jerry Smallwood, 39, was shot by Mounties numerous times after he fatally shot himself. Now, a coroner's inquest will try to learn more.
article: A coroner's inquest into the fatal 2018 police shooting at Departure Bay ferry terminal got underway in Nanaimo on Tuesday.
On May 8, 2018, Nanaimo RCMP undercover units boxed in a car as it drove off a BC Ferry at Departure Bay in Nanaimo.
Shots then rang out as the man inside raised a gun to his head and shot himself, and two officers also shot him numerous times.
"Within minutes, everything took place. The bang, the gunshots," one witness told CHEK News at the scene that day.
"It was a loud bang like an explosion," said another man.
"And then I heard three, maybe four smaller shots after that," added a third witness.

A subsequent report by the Independent Investigations Office of B.C. concluded the officers were not at fault and that the victim, Jerry Smallwood, who turned 39 years old that day, had fatally shot himself first.
Now, six-and-a-half years later, a coroner's inquest into the shooting death has commenced in Nanaimo to learn more about what happened.
The victim's mother, Sharon Smallwood, was the first to testify, starting off by saying Jerry had a normal, happy upbringing in Winnipeg.
"Jerry was a happy little boy," she read from a prepared statement.
She said in later years, he had suffered a back injury at work that led to prescription drugs that led to him using street drugs.
She said her son became depressed, "dealing with the pain and dealing with Worker's Compensation."
She said WorkSafeBC had stopped his payments and that her son had been fighting with WorkSafeBC for 2.5 years leading up to his death.
Kelowna family physician Dr. Andre Hugo testified that he had first seen Jerry as a patient on Dec. 22, 2015, after Jerry had suffered a "slip and fall injury" that had occurred in October.
Two specialists had determined that surgery was not the best treatment.
Jerry was prescribed pain medication as well as anti-depressants.
Dr. Hugo testified that Jerry later "self-discontinued" his anti-depressants and suffered withdrawal symptoms.
He was aware of Jerry's cannabis use and did not approve.

A later witness, Danielle Frost, who was Jerry's girlfriend in 2018 in Salmon Arm, testified that he had said he couldn't afford the prescription drugs and wasn't trying to get high on the illicit drugs but was just trying to deal with the pain.
Both his mother and Frost said the drugs had changed Jerry, and Frost said she was "fearful of him and his anger."
The inquest heard that he was having a dispute with a drug dealer in Vernon and that he told Frost on the night of May 7, 2018, that he had "wasted someone in a parking lot."
His next call to Frost came later that night after he said he had tried to steal someone's car in Penticton after his car ran out of gas.
The next day, he ended up at the Departure Bay terminal, where police tracked him to the ferry as he was a suspect in a violent carjacking in Penticton.
As he drove off the ferry at 10:15 a.m., they boxed him in, and the shooting occurred.
Frost told the inquest that Jerry had told her the day before: "I'm not going to jail, police will have to shoot me."
The inquest heard that Jerry had once lived on Vancouver Island and liked it, which is why he might have been trying to escape to the area.
Under Section 18(2) of the Coroners Act, inquests are mandatory for any deaths that occur while a person was detained by or in the custody of a peace officer.

A coroner's inquest is a public inquiry that serves three primary functions: to determine the facts related to a death, including the identity of the deceased; and how, when, where and by what means the individual came to their death, as well as a classification for the death; to make recommendations, where appropriate and supported by evidence, to prevent deaths in similar circumstances; and to ensure public confidence that the circumstances surrounding the death of an individual will not be overlooked, concealed or ignored.
The inquest is expected to hear from 23 witnesses and wrap up on Monday.
